description: `cli-health search "<query>"` returns ranked commands across all adopting scenarios in AI mode; `--text` fallback operates without Ollama or Qdrant.

requirements.description: The `cli-health search "<query>"` command (default mode) must embed the query using the `nomic-embed-text` model via Ollama, query the Qdrant vector store for the top-K nearest command embeddings across all indexed scenarios, and return results ranked by cosine similarity. Results must include at minimum: command name, scenario name, short description, and similarity score. The command must achieve recall@5 ≥ 0.8 on the hand-labeled query corpus stored at `scenarios/cli-health/testdata/search_queries.json`.
requirements.title: AI Semantic Search via Qdrant and nomic-embed-text

validation.notes: Given a mocked Ollama embed response and mocked Qdrant search response, search returns results sorted descending by similarity score
Given a Qdrant result set, the output includes command name, scenario name, description, and score for each hit
Unit test for the manifest scan discovery source: given a synthetic manifest, all non-omitted commands are emitted as indexable documents
Embedded integration test with real Qdrant and real Ollama: index a known command set, run 5 representative queries, assert top result is the expected command

Recall@5 evaluation test: run all ~20 queries from search_queries.json against a populated index and assert recall@5 ≥ 0.8. HARNESS: api/internal/aisearch/recall_test.go::TestCommandRecall (live-gated by CLI_HEALTH_AISEARCH_LIVE=1; rebuilds a dedicated collection with the production read policy). DEEP INVESTIGATION 2026-06-07 (measured matrix; see experiment_test.go / retrieval_diag_test.go / bvariants_test.go / final_test.go): recall improved 0.50 → 0.70 (14/20) and the remaining gap is now fully root-caused. WHAT MOVED IT (measured, shipped): (1) nomic task prefixes — embedding queries with 'search_query:' and passages with 'search_document:' lifts canonical commands up the RAW retrieval (e.g. 'vrooli scenario list' #17→#2, 'create a record' #32→#4); opt-in via CLI_HEALTH_EMBED_TASK_PREFIX. (2) RRF rerank BLEND — the cross-encoder was the single biggest recall destroyer (it pure-reordered, promoting literal-token siblings; rerank-ON=0.50 vs rerank-OFF=0.70). Blending its order with retrieval (CLI_HEALTH_RERANK_BLEND) recovers full recall AND keeps junk rejection (gibberish stays ~0.03/weak; pure rerank-off leaked 5 strong junk hits). WHAT DID NOT HELP (measured, NOT shipped): enriched embedding text (0.70→0.40, hurts), hybrid sparse leg (mixed/negative on this corpus), canonical-origin authority boost (0.70→0.65, hurts). THE REMAINING 6 MISSES are NOT retrieval-algorithm problems: (a) 'git-control-tower baseline snapshot' — a REAL command but git-control-tower's cli/manifest.json declares only the 'worktree' group, so manifest-first discovery never indexes the baseline group (filed: GCT manifest-completeness bug); (b) 'vrooli help' — NOT a discrete command ('--help' is a flag); the 'show available commands' label tests a non-command (filed); (c) 'prompt-manager action create' — now INDEXED after fixing the help-parser to handle 'create, add  <desc>' alias rows (helpparser.go commandLineRE), but still ranks just outside top-5 (genuine vocab gap register↔create); (d) 'cli-health search query/status' + 'app-issue-tracker issue create' — indexed, ranked just outside top-5 (vocab gap / sibling competition). Labels were NOT rewritten to match engine output (no gaming). Status stays in_progress: hitting 0.8 needs the GCT manifest fix (+1) plus a retrieval gain on the ~3 vocab-gap cases (a stronger embed model or per-command synonyms — measured: terse text + prefixes + blend is the best config found so far).
AI search returns results within an acceptable latency budget on a warm local stack (no explicit cap defined for AI mode; cap applies to --text mode only)
Developers can discover CLI commands across scenarios using natural language without knowing exact command names

requirements.description: When `cli-health search "<query>" --text` is specified, or when Ollama or Qdrant are unavailable, the command must fall back to a pure text-based search over command names, descriptions, and flag metadata loaded directly from manifest files. No network calls to Ollama or Qdrant may be made in this mode. Results must be returned in under 2 seconds on a cold local stack. The `--text` flag must be explicitly documented in the command help output.
requirements.title: Text-mode Search Fallback Without Ollama or Qdrant

validation.notes: Given --text flag, the Qdrant and Ollama clients are never invoked
Given a set of synthetic manifests and a query matching a command description substring, --text search returns that command in results
Given --text flag, results are ranked by relevance heuristic (e.g., term frequency or string similarity score)
Run `cli-health search "create user" --text` with Ollama and Qdrant services stopped; assert nonzero results returned and exit code 0
Measure wall-clock time for --text search across all 6 adopting scenarios on a cold stack and assert < 2s
--text search must return results in < 2 seconds on a cold local stack with all adopting scenario manifests loaded
Teams without GPU/Ollama infrastructure can still use CLI discovery; CI pipelines without AI services remain functional

title: Semantic and text-mode command search
